summary: Shinshu Kusumoto specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Shoryu Katsura, having also studied under Hideyo Ogawa, Hiromi Yoshimura, Kazufumi Oki, Osamu Hayashima, and Tomoyuki Uno.

Shintaro Kitano is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under supervisor Kazunobu Matsuda (attested 2005). He held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 2005) and Kyushu University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).
Shinten Sakai (1912–1989) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Shindo Shiraishi and held a post at Koyasan University (attested 1959).

Shinya Moriyama is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1996–1998) and earned his Dr.Phil at the University of Vienna (~2002–2006), later holding a post at Shinshu University around 2009.
Shinya Yasutomi (1944–2017) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1964–1968). He served as a professor at Otani University from around 1985 to 2015.

Shiro Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo under Zuiho Yamaguchi and Yasuaki Nara, he was a professor at Komazawa University (~1993–2016) and visited the University of Chicago (~1998–1999).

Shivaram Dattatray Joshi (1926–2013) worked in Indology and linguistics, studying under Shankashastri Marulkar, Maheshwarshastri Joshi, and Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He was a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1967–1992) and headed Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College (attested 1996).

Shizuka Sasaki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1975–1984) under Jikido Takasaki. He served as Professor of Indian Buddhism at Hanazono University from around 1990 to 2021.

Shlomo Pines (1908–1990) specialized in philosophy, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1926–1927) and held a post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem from around 1952 to 1986.
Shobha Rani Dash specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She held posts as a researcher at Ryukoku University in 2010 and as a lecturer at Otani University (attested 2012).
Shodo Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami and Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University (attested 1995–2013).

Shodo Yamagami is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1962–1964) and served as an assistant professor at Kyoto Sangyo University from around 1970 to 2010.
Shogo Watanabe specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Toyo University (~1972–1981) and later held posts there, serving as a professor from around 2000 to 2019.

Shohaku Okumura is a Buddhist studies specialist who studied at Komazawa University (~1968–1972) and under Kosho Uchiyama (1972–1975). He was interim head teacher at Minnesota Zen Meditation Center (1993–1996) and director at Soto Zen Buddhism International Center (1997, ~1997–2010).

Shoji Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University under Giyu Nishi. He held posts at the Okura Institute (~1971–1980) and Toyo University as assistant professor (~1979–1989) and professor (~1989–2009).
Shoju Inaba (1915–1990) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a professor at Otani University (~1957–1985) and worked as a part-time lecturer at Nagoya University.

Shojun Bando (1932–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1957). He held posts at Ueno Gakuen University, Komazawa University (attested 1974), and Otani University (~1977–1998).
Shoko Kanaoka (1930–1987) was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He held academic posts as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1987, 2000).
Shoko Miyabayashi (1932–2014) specialized in Buddhist studies. He studied at Taisho University from around 1951 to 1961 and later held a post there from around 1978 to 2003.
Shoko Takeuchi (1910–1999) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served at Ryukoku University as an emeritus professor (attested 1987–1995, 2009).
